_table: Notice to cure or quit: non-monetary breach cure period
_note: basis as above; days = 0 means no statutory pre-suit cure window.
_notice: General reference, not legal advice. Statutes change and vary by jurisdiction; verify every figure against the current official state code before relying on it. Last reviewed 2026-05.

AK.citation: Alaska Stat. § 34.03.220(a)(1) (cure within 10; lease terminates day 30 if uncured)

CA.citation: Cal. Civ. Proc. Code § 1161(3): excludes Saturdays, Sundays, judicial holidays; non-curable breaches use Cal. Civ. Proc. Code § 1161(4) Notice to Quit

DC.citation: D.C. Code § 42-3505.01(b) (30-day cure for most lease violations)

GA.citation: O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50 (no statutory cure window; lease terms control)

IA.citation: Iowa Code § 562A.27 (curable); 3 days for material clear-and-present-danger

MO.citation: Mo. Rev. Stat. § 441.060 (10-day notice for breach)

MS.citation: Miss. Code § 89-8-13(3) (cure within 14 days or terminate)

NH.citation: N.H. Rev. Stat. § 540:3 (30-day notice for substantial breach)

NJ.citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(d) and 2A:18-61.2 (notice-to-cease required; no statutory cure period: continued conduct after cease triggers eviction)

NM.citation: N.M.S.A. § 47-8-33(B) (7-day cure for substantial violation; 3-day for material safety)

NY.citation: NY RPAPL § 753(4) (10-day post-judgment cure right + lease typically provides 30-day pre-suit cure)

OH.citation: Ohio Rev. Code § 5321.11 (30-day notice; lease may shorten)

OK.citation: Okla. Stat. tit. 41 § 132 (15-day cure for breach)

OR.citation: ORS 90.392 (30-day cure for material noncompliance; 24-hour for outrageous conduct)

PA.citation: 68 P.S. § 250.501(b) (15-day notice for breach of conditions, lease <= 1 yr)

TN.citation: Tenn. Code § 66-28-505 (14-day cure; 30 days to vacate)

TX.citation: Tex. Prop. Code § 24.005 (default; lease may shorten or lengthen)

VA.citation: Va. Code § 55.1-1245(C) (21/30: 21-day cure; lease terminates 30 days if uncured)

WI.citation: Wis. Stat. § 704.17(1p)(b) (5-day cure for breach other than rent)

WV.citation: W. Va. Code § 55-3A-1 (no statutory pre-suit cure; lease terms control)
